correctness.rationale: For n even, Lucas submask restrictions and Narayana symmetry yield 2^{s2(n)} odd entries. For n odd, adjacent binary submask pairs sit in blocks of 2^t consecutive indices (t=ν2(n+1)), yielding 2^{s2(n)-t}(2^t−1). Counting free higher bits gives exact multiset over every dyadic range; the even-row and odd-row contributions sum to (5·3^(L−1)−3)/2. Independent exact integer computations checked all rows 1..256 and complete dyadic spectra L1..9. This is an infinite combinatorial proof, not finite extrapolation.
